summary.headline: The Southborough School Committee reorganized leadership, renewed its food service contract with Whitsons, and reviewed bus operations and capital roof projects.
summary.summary: Following the town election, the Southborough School Committee welcomed a new member and reorganized leadership, electing a chair, vice chair, and secretary. The committee approved extending its food services contract with Whitsons Culinary Group for the 2026-2027 school year, which includes a 3.9% fee increase. Administration also updated the committee on improved school bus operations and security camera monitoring, kindergarten enrollment projections, and the timeline for summer bidding on the Neary School roof replacement project.

topics.title: School Committee reorganization and officer elections
topics.summary: Following the annual town election, the committee reorganized its officer positions and representatives to Superintendency Union 3. Members voted to re-elect Chelsea Malinowski as chair, Laura Kauffman as vice chair, and newly elected member Kelly as secretary.
key_details: Chelsea Malinowski was nominated and approved as chair.
Laura Kauffman was nominated and approved as vice chair.
Kelly was nominated and approved as secretary.
Three committee members were designated to serve on Superintendency Union 3.
topics.outcome: New committee officers and union representatives approved.

topics.title: Elementary Building Committee update
topics.summary: The superintendent reported that the Select Board voted on May 5 to approve Tappe as the designer for the elementary building project. The committee is now negotiating the contract and planning the kickoff meeting to envision the future of Neary Elementary School.
key_details: Select Board approved designer selection of Tappe on May 5.
Contract negotiations with Tappe are underway.
The project will address long-term planning for Neary Elementary School.
topics.outcome: Contract negotiations ongoing with design firm Tappe.

topics.title: Whitsons food service contract renewal and financial update
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the financial and operational status of its first year with Whitsons Culinary Group and voted to extend the contract for the 2026-2027 school year. The food service program showed a net loss of $58,939 through March 2026, driven largely by a one-time transfer of $57,900 for employee health insurance, increased administrative staffing, and mandatory training days. The renewal includes a 3.9% increase tied to the Consumer Price Index, adjusting the administrative fee to 5.2 cents per meal and the management fee to 12.1 cents per meal, while maintaining a guaranteed return provision.
key_details: Net loss through Q3 was $58,939, driven in part by $57,900 in employee health insurance shifted to the revolving fund.
The contract guarantees a return of $19,312 or Whitsons must cover the deficit difference.
Renewal includes a 3.9% CPI adjustment, moving the administrative fee to 5.2 cents per meal and management fee to 12.1 cents.
Administration will review Whitsons performance in December to determine whether to rebid or continue the contract in year three.
topics.outcome: Approved extending the Whitsons food service contract for the 2026-2027 school year.
topics.why_it_matters: Directly affects school operating budgets, cafeteria program quality, and food service costs for Southborough public schools.

topics.title: Transportation operations and technology update
topics.summary: Staff provided an update on bus operations with NRT, noting that driver staffing and service reliability have stabilized significantly since the fall. Upgrades including turn-by-turn GPS and live bus security camera access have been implemented, though rollout of student RFID tap cards has experienced delays. The superintendent noted the district is assessing contractual penalties to withhold payment for technology features that were delayed or non-operational.
key_details: Live bus camera feeds have been operational and accessible to school administrators since mid-January.
RFID student scanning has faced implementation delays due to driver training and hardware issues.
District administration is pursuing contract penalty deductions from NRT for delayed technology deliverables.
Bus registration opt-in for the 2026-2027 school year will open with a target registration deadline of June 12.
topics.outcome: Information accepted; administration to meet with NRT in June regarding penalty adjustments.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee accepted a commercial donation, approved warrants and payroll, reviewed revolving accounts, accepted personnel changes, and approved multiple past meeting minutes.
key_details: Accepted a $354.70 donation from Ahold Delhaize USA to Trottier Middle School.
Approved warrants and payroll.
Reviewed balances for food services, facility rental, extended day, and preschool revolving funds.
Approved open session minutes for February 26, March 2, March 31, April 2, April 8, and April 11, 2026.

topics.title: Student Support Services director restructuring
topics.summary: The district announced a restructuring of the Central Office Director of Student Support Services position into three separate district-based director roles for Northborough, Southborough, and Algonquin. The committee appointed a member to participate in the screening and interview committee for the Southborough position.
key_details: The single district-wide director position is being replaced by three individual district directors.
Algonquin promoted an internal candidate, while Northborough and Southborough are conducting parallel searches.
Roger Challen was appointed to represent the Southborough School Committee on the screening panel.
topics.outcome: Roger Challen appointed to the candidate screening committee.

topics.title: Capital projects and Neary roof replacement timeline
topics.summary: Following voter approval at Annual Town Meeting and the town election for roof projects at Neary and Trottier schools, staff reviewed project timelines. Bids for the Neary roof project are due May 22, with approximately 8 to 10 contractors having attended the site visit. Contract award is anticipated around June 10, with construction scheduled to begin immediately following the end of the school year.
key_details: Neary roof replacement bids are due on May 22.
Eight to 10 contractors attended the pre-bid site walkthrough.
The committee expects to award the bid at its June 10 meeting.
Construction is targeted to start immediately after classes end in June.
topics.outcome: Bids due May 22; contract award expected at the June 10 meeting.

topics.title: Enrollment and class size projections
topics.summary: The superintendent presented current enrollment figures, highlighting 116 registered kindergarten students projected into six sections for the 2026-2027 school year. First grade is projected to have seven sections with an average class size of approximately 17 students. The district is holding open one unallocated elementary teaching position in reserve in case late kindergarten registrations require adding a seventh section.
key_details: Kindergarten registration stands at 116 students across six planned sections.
First grade will feature seven sections averaging roughly 17 students per class.
A retired teacher's position is being held open as contingency if kindergarten exceeds capacity.

topics.title: FY26 budget report and line-item transfers
topics.summary: The committee approved the monthly general fund expenditure report through April 30, 2026, and approved line-item budget transfers. As of April 30, the district had an unencumbered balance of $221,522, representing less than 1% of the operating budget. The superintendent reported the receipt of $201,400 in unexpected state Circuit Breaker extraordinary relief funds due to prior special education costs, which will help ease special education pressures in the FY27 budget.
key_details: Unencumbered operating budget balance was $221,522.27 as of April 30, 2026.
District received $201,400.47 in state Circuit Breaker relief funds.
Approved transfers to balance accounts for audit expenses ($1,000), student activity stipends ($2,578), and electricity costs.
Electricity line items were adjusted due to higher winter heating and power consumption.
topics.outcome: Approved the monthly financial report and line-item budget transfers.
topics.why_it_matters: Ensures town schools close out the fiscal year within legal budget appropriations and tracks taxpayer funds.
